newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian March CPI - 0.09 vs +1.54 in February.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian March CPI - 0.09 vs +1.54 in February.

text.p: The Palestinian consumer price index (CPI) in the West Bank and Gaza Strip fell 0.09 percent in March compared to a 1.54 percent rise in February, the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics (PCBS) said on Tuesday.
The PCBS said in a statement that the index (base 100=1996) was 106.25 in March 1997 compared with 101.24 in March 1996.

The statement attributed March's drop to a 1.63 percent decline in food prices and a 0.26 percent drop in transport costs. Housing prices rose 1.23 percent while education costs rose 1.38 percent, the PCBS said in a statement.

The PCBS said the sharpest drop was in the West Bank, where prices fell 0.37 percent. In the Gaza Strip, prices dropped 0.27 percent while in East Jerusalem prices rose 0.52 percent, the statement said.

The PCBS, which began issuing data in November 1995, calculates prices in the three areas separately due to the geographic division between them. The Palestinian Authority controls only part of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, while East Jerusalem remains under Israeli rule.
